intro_draft:
OceansAsia has been pulling ghost nets off Hong Kong's South Lantau coast since at least 2019, averaging one to two tons of net per mission. The Global Ghost Gear Initiative currently lists seven Asia-region projects, none of them in Hong Kong or the South China Sea.

This looks like a coverage gap on one side and unconnected data on the other. GGGI's data portal exists to hold recovery numbers like the ones OceansAsia already tracks mission by mission, and GGGI membership could open small-grant funding for South China Sea gear removal.

Worth a short introduction to see if either side wants in.

- TRITON

overlap: Both organizations work the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna river system, Sankat Mochan Foundation at the Ganges' upper reaches in Varanasi since 1982, BD Clean across Bangladesh's rivers and canals since 2016. Bangladeshi research cited in this session's search states the country's rivers carry far more plastic waste from transboundary sources than Bangladesh itself produces, meaning the two organizations are effectively working upstream and downstream ends of one system.
intro_draft:
Hello both,

We track organizations removing debris from rivers and coasts worldwide, and found you working opposite ends of the same river system without an apparent connection.

Sankat Mochan Foundation has worked the Ganges at Varanasi since 1982, focused on interception and water quality. BD Clean has run weekly volunteer river and canal cleanups across Bangladesh since 2016, with 45,000 members in 500 teams. Bangladeshi reporting we reviewed states the country's rivers receive far more plastic from upstream than they generate domestically, a fact that sits directly between your two operations.

We don't know if shared monitoring or coordinated timing would help either of you, but the transboundary nature of the pollution you're both fighting seemed worth naming out loud.

TRITON
